title: Yakisoba Stir Fried Wheat Noodles

description: Yakisoba is a beloved Japanese stir-fried noodle dish, packed with savory flavors and vibrant vegetables. Chewy wheat noodles are tossed with tender meat, crisp cabbage, and a rich, tangy sauce, creating a perfectly balanced and satisfying meal. It's a popular street food and home-cooked favorite, bringing a taste of Japan to your kitchen.

ingredients.item: Pork belly or thinly sliced pork

instructions.title: Prepare the Yakisoba Noodles
instructions.text: If using fresh Yakisoba noodles, loosen them under hot water or briefly blanch in boiling water for 30 seconds, then drain well. If using dried chuka soba, cook according to package directions until al dente, then rinse with cold water and drain thoroughly to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Prepare the Yakisoba Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together 4 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, and 1/2 tsp ground black pepper. This is your homemade Yakisoba sauce. Set aside.

instructions.title: Cook the Pork
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the thinly sliced pork and stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes. Remove the pork from the pan and set aside, leaving any rendered fat in the pan.

instructions.title: Stir-fry the Vegetables
instructions.text: Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the same pan. Add the sliced onion and julienned carrot and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened. Add the sliced cabbage and continue to stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes until the cabbage is tender-crisp.

instructions.title: Combine Noodles, Pork, and Sauce
instructions.text: Return the cooked pork to the pan with the vegetables. Add the prepared Yakisoba noodles. Pour the Yakisoba sauce evenly over the noodles and ingredients. Using tongs or two spatulas, toss everything together vigorously until the noodles and all ingredients are well coated with the sauce and heated through, about 3-4 minutes.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Once the noodles are thoroughly mixed and hot, transfer the Yakisoba to serving plates. Garnish generously with chopped scallions and a sprinkle of benishoga (pickled red ginger) if desired. Serve immediately and enjoy!

tips: To achieve authentic wok-hei (smoky flavor), use a very hot wok and cook ingredients in batches if your pan is not large enough to avoid steaming the vegetables.
For a vegetarian version, omit the pork and oyster sauce, and add more vegetables like bell peppers, mushrooms, or bean sprouts. Use a vegetarian Worcestershire sauce.
Yakisoba is best served immediately. If you have leftovers, store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan or microwave.
